findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following date marking issues:

(1) Cooked turkey in the walk-in cooler that was prepared on 12/30/2025. CORRECTED - The PIC noticed it was on old date mark and they put the correct date on the turkey container. 

(2) Ranch made in-house in the walk-in cooler that was prepared on 12/31/2025. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed that the ranch was held past the seven day date marking period and it was discarded during the inspection.  

(3) Oat milk at the bar that was opened on Sunday was not date marked. CORRECTED: The PIC date marked the oat milk during the inspection. 

Ensure that all ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the seven day maximum and that food is discarded after seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following non-food contact surfaces to have accumulation of dust and food residue:
- The top of the heat lamp has an accumulation of dust.
- The gap between the oven and fryer has accumulation of food residue and grease on the floor.
- The shelves in the walk-in cooler have accumulation of debris.
- The fan casing in the walk-in cooler have accumulation of dust.

PIC was informed and cleaning will be done before the next routine inspection. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of dirt, dust, food residue or other debris by cleaning regularly to prevent potential food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed some of the employees food handlers certificates to have expired. PIC was informed. Ensure all employees handling foods obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed the waitress making a drink at the bar placed an ice cube into a drink with their bare hands. The employee was instructed to dump the drink and re-make it when the action was observed. The PIC was informed and they showed the waitress the location of the tongs that are used to transfer ice to the drinks. Ensure that ready-to-eat foods are never handled with bare hands.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the fry station prep cooler was holding foods above 41F. The following internal temperatures were recorded: lettuce 53F, spring mix 50F, lettuce 49F, mozzarella cheese 47F, cooked chicken 50F, diced tomatoes 48F, sausage 48F, raw chicken 47F, and raw fish 47F. The internal hanging thermometer was reading at about 50F. When the temperatures were originally observed out of range the inspector gave the cooler 30 minutes to cool down after lunch. However, after 30 minutes the cooler was still above 41F. The PIC stated that all foods had been inside the cooler for over four hours. All temperature control for safety (TCS) foods were voluntarily discarded during the inspection (foods referenced above). There was two containers of tofu that were within the safety range and moved immediately to a functioning cooler. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (pickles, onions, lemons, bread etc.). During the inspection the PIC called to schedule service. The PIC was instructed that TCS foods cannot be stored inside the cooler until it is functioning. The facility will be either using time-as-control or ice baths until it is serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 6/10/2205 (the facility is closed on Mondays) to check on the temperature of the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the underside of the shelves above the prep cooler in the fry station have an accumulation of grease, food debris, and other residues. The PIC was shown the location that needs to be cleaned. Ensure that the underside of the shelves are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil resides.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces need to be cleaned: (1) Dust on the walk-in cooler fans; and (2) Grease in between the fryers on the cook line. Ensure these areas are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil resides.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed an employee storing their cell phone on a shelf adjacent to the pizza & salad prep cooler holding clean plates and utensils. The employee was educated and they removed their phone from the location. Ensure that personal items are stored away from food prep areas to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee touch ready-to-eat-food with their bare hand. The employee also had an open wound on their hand that was not gloved. Inspectors had a discussion with the PIC and advised covering the wound and keeping it gloved. Inspectors also advised that the employee should work in an area not pertaining to food to prevent contamination of food.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed interior cavity of kitchen ice machine to be soiled with debris. Clean and sanitize interior cavity of kitchen ice machine. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed bottom of containers used to store clean cooking utensils to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize storage containers for cooking utensils. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed nozzle of soda gun on left side of bar to be soiled with debris. Clean and sanitize nozzle of soda gun. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed wet mop heads to be stored down in mop bucket. Store wet mop heads in a fashion that promotes drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several cans of ketchup which were dented and had already been stocked in. All dented cans were removed by person-in-charge. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
There is some condensation dripping from the condenser unit of the walk-in freezer. Due to the use of the freezer for cooling small items, these foods must be located away from any dripping condensation at all times or otherwise protected from contamination. No obvious contamination was observed. Foods were removed from underneath the units. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

3-305.12: FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (B) In toilet rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G) Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H) Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the hand sink at the front of the kitchen had ice in it. Hand sinks may only be used for hand washing. Dumping of any kind, including water/ice is not allowed. Ensure that hand washing sinks remain available and easily accessible at all times.

The hand sink at the back of the facility did not have paper towels available. The automatic paper towel dispenser was empty. Person-in-charge replaced the paper towels and discussed with employee the need to monitor paper towels and replace as necessary. Corrected on site. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed several cups sitting in flour containers being used as scoops in flour containers and a sugar container in the kitchen. Ensure that appropriate scoops are used and are stored handle up to prevent bare-hand contact with food. Scoops/cups may also be stored on clean, dry surfaces when not being used. Cups were removed from containers by person-in-charge. Corrected on site. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.
